niche: the Scotland field region of a home heating repair and boiler cover company: which cause of missed two-hour appointments to fix before the January breakdown peak, when the summer's leading cause is generated by an out-of-hours arrangement the winter season replaces
answer: Parts & van stock is the cause that will be behind the most missed appointments over January to March if nothing changes, 322 of the July to September 2026 misses; put the vans back on weekly top-ups before January. Rota & cover led the quarter (571) but stops over the winter, when the contractor panel takes the evening calls standby cannot reach (no Rota & cover miss in any month October 2025 to May 2026); runner-up over the peak Engineer attendance & punctuality, 246.

driver: The decisive quantity is which measured cause still operates in the forward window the decision buys: the largest cause in the closed quarter arises only when overflow work lands on the primary workforce late in the day, and a second provider layer that the coming season brings back takes that overflow whole, so the ranking every attribution of the closed quarter reproduces does not carry into the window, and the cause that carries is the quarter's runner-up, whose driver the season leaves untouched.
driver_concrete: Q3 missed appointments trace across the day boundary to the eleven-hour rest after evening call-outs that day-roster engineers took while the standby pool was short, so Rota & cover leads Q3; but from October to May the out-of-hours desk passes the evening calls standby cannot reach to the contractor panel, no day-roster engineer clears late and the rest never moves a log-on, so over January to March the cause that costs the most is the van top-up change, the Q3 runner-up.
stump: A competent solver traces each July to September missed appointment across the day boundary to the previous evening's out-of-hours call-out, charges the largest share to Rota & cover, and names it for the January peak because winter out-of-hours demand runs half as high again as the summer's while the standby pool is down to six; the step that lands it there is never asking where last winter's evening overflow went, which the out-of-hours log answers: from October to May the calls standby could not reach went to the contractor panel, no day-roster engineer cleared a call-out after 20:40, and the rest never moved a log-on.

differentiation.task86: task86 runs an earlier scheduled draw forward member by member so a shared pool is depleted before the decision's draw; nothing is depleted here: a seasonal second provider takes over the overflow work that generates the closed quarter's leading cause, so the cause ranking itself differs between the measured quarter and the window the decision buys.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is the share of failures whose originating delay sits in work done in an earlier period under a different system, reached by joining each resource's first event of a period to the end of its previous period's work through an identifier crosswalk and applying a mandatory minimum gap, because the delayed start the record attributes to the resource's own conduct is forced by off-schedule work, so an analysis that traces each failure back along the period to its first late event files the resource's conduct as the cause.
lineage.driver_concrete: Q3 missed appointments trace along each engineer's day to a late log-on, and those late log-ons are the 11 hours' rest the working-time policy requires after an evening emergency call-out that a day-roster engineer took because the standby pool was short, a call-out held only in the out-of-hours system under payroll numbers, so the cause is out-of-hours cover rather than punctuality, routing or slot design.
lineage.stump: A competent solver traces each Q3 missed appointment back along the engineer's day, finds most chains start with a log-on after the rostered start, codes those to engineer punctuality exactly as the verified first-half sample does, sets the July routing upgrade aside on the travel figures, and files punctuality as the cause; the step that lands it there is never asking why those engineers logged on late, which the previous evening's out-of-hours call-out finish plus the 11-hour rest answers every time.
lineage.fate: solved on the portal (author's report 2026-10-06): both responses filed the golden, Rota & cover, 449 of 1,288; the decisive rung (the rest after an evening call-out, reached through the payroll crosswalk) was conceded by the punctuality family's 'within the engineer's own control' clause, and the graded quantity was an argmax over a filed family list; re-rooted at stage 1 onto the forward window
